title: Soccar
mechanics: Rocket-powered car soccer. The accessible Free Play mode places a car and soccer ball in an arena; this pass verified forward movement but did not test scoring or a competitive match.

actions: Selected the visible Free Play option from the title screen.
Held W for 600 ms in the arena.
gameplay.outcome: Free Play loaded with a car, ball, arena, and 0–0 scoreboard. After W, the arena/car viewpoint shifted forward; no goal was scored and the scoreboard remained 0–0. Escape toggled the menu display but was not needed for the movement check.
limitations: Only Free Play movement was checked; competitive play, ball contact, and scoring were not verified.

sources.detail: Loaded the live title screen and Free Play arena; screenshot shows a car, soccer ball, arena, and score HUD.

rationale: Sports is the best fit for the car-soccer rules/activity visible in Free Play. The tested route was explicitly Free Play, so this evidence does not establish a human multiplayer mode.

title: STARFALL: The Last Beacon
mechanics: Campaign space shooter: fly through hostile waves, fire weapons, protect hull, and advance through short scored mission stages. The first-party field guide lists WASD/arrows to move, W/up to boost, Space/J to fire, and 13 steps in Mission 1.

actions: Read the in-game How to Play field guide for keyboard controls.
Launched the mission again, held W for 900 ms, then held Space for 1,200 ms.
gameplay.outcome: The mission HUD began at hull 100, score 000000, progress 1/13. After the movement/fire inputs it showed hull 8, score 000200, and progress 3/13. An earlier no-input run ended at Signal Lost with score 0; this was not treated as a success.
limitations: Only the first mission was tested; no mission completion or multiplayer mode was observed.

sources.detail: Campaign menu frames the game around firing through waves and lighting three beacons; the live mission exposes hull, score, and 1/13 progression.
In-game guide states WASD/arrows move, W/up boosts, Space/J fires primary weapon, and describes three campaign beacons and mission controls.

rationale: Action describes the real-time shooter combat, while Arcade fits its short wave-and-score mission loop. Narrative framing alone does not justify Adventure over those observed mechanics.

title: The Street Game
mechanics: Marbles game against the named AI opponent Claude. The first-party page instructs the player to drag backward and release to shoot; the scoreboard identifies YOU and CLAUDE.

actions: Opened the title screen, selected Play, and restarted the round using the visible Play Again control.
Followed the on-screen instruction and dragged backward across the board before releasing.
gameplay.outcome: The live page presented a marbles board and the drag/release instruction. After the drag, the screenshot showed a marbles formation without the animated hand, but the score remained 0–0 and the page continued to expose a stale GAME OVER overlay, so this run did not establish a reliable current round-state change. A prior local direct-play receipt reports a visible shot/formation response against Claude, while explicitly claiming no point, win, or completed round.
limitations: The current run's GAME OVER overlay appeared stale; no score or completed round was observed. Prior gameplay evidence is cited separately, not represented as this run's verification.

sources.detail: The live page presents a marble board, YOU-versus-CLAUDE score, and drag-back/release-to-shoot instruction.
Reports a visible board/shot-marble response after drag-and-release against Claude; score stayed 0–0 and no win/completed round was claimed.

rationale: The title presents a casual marbles-versus-AI activity. Casual remains the most defensible existing category; no multiplayer tag is appropriate for an AI opponent, and this pass did not establish a distinct sports/arcade loop strongly enough to change the tag.

title: Time Echo
mechanics: First-person exploration in a repeating room/cycle. The game says actions persist across resets and tracks memories to find; the loop combines exploration with observation and temporal puzzle solving.

actions: Selected Enter/continue from the paused Empty Room screen.
Held W for 1,000 ms during the first recording cycle.
Clicked the room view to capture mouse/look control and allowed the timed cycle to continue; then held W for another 700 ms.
gameplay.outcome: The initial paused state showed Cycle 01 and Memories 0/1. The recording run proceeded through resets; a later live view showed Cycle 03, Memories 1/1, and the in-game message 'The room is the same. What happens is not.' This verifies a changing cycle/memory state, though the test did not isolate which movement or timing event discovered the memory.
limitations: The cause of the 0/1-to-1/1 memory change was not isolated, and no later level was tested.

sources.detail: The live screen states that cycles reset while some actions persist and displays cycle and memory counters, with WASD/mouse look controls.

rationale: Adventure covers first-person environmental exploration and progression through cycles; Puzzle is a meaningful secondary tag because discovering persistent memories through repeated cycles is the stated core mechanic.

title: Ttak! Stop
mechanics: Single-player timing/reflex score game: start the moving marker and stop it inside the colored target zone for points; misses trigger a death effect.

actions: Clicked the canvas at the visible Tap to start prompt.
Pressed Space once to stop the marker.
gameplay.outcome: The live screen changed from a 0-score round with marker and target bar to a red particle/death animation after Space; score was not readable in the live capture. A prior local direct-play receipt separately reports a successful stop (score 0 to 152) and a target-zone move. No leaderboard submission or challenge sharing was attempted.
limitations: This live press appears to have missed and did not expose a readable score; the successful score result is from the prior receipt.

sources.detail: The live canvas says Tap/Space to stop and displays the target zone; the Korean subtitle describes bar color changes with score and a death effect.
Reports a timing round where Space changed score 0 to 152 and moved the target zone.

rationale: Arcade fits a repeatable reaction/timing score challenge. A leaderboard or share/challenge button does not establish multiplayer.

title: Void Explorer
mechanics: Spaceflight/navigation simulator in a procedural universe. The HUD models thrust, velocity, planet range, arrival time, flight profile, and surface altitude; the expedition menu advertises 2,048 reachable systems.

actions: Selected Start Expedition from the launch screen.
Held Space for 1,500 ms to apply thrust.
gameplay.outcome: The live flight HUD changed from velocity 0.0 m/s, Aurelia Veil range 11,782 km, and arrival 1m39s to 108 km/s, 11,593 km, and 1m36s after thrust.
limitations: Only short-range flight was tested; approach, landing, on-foot exploration, and other systems were not tested.

sources.detail: Launch and flight HUD describe an explorable procedural universe, ship thrust, navigation, planet range, speed, and arrival estimates; the current short flight reproduced changing telemetry.
Prior direct-play receipt independently confirms Space thrust changes velocity and destination range; its values differ slightly from this current short test.

rationale: Use the displayed site taxonomy name Simulators (the catalog uses Simulation as an alias). Measured flight and navigation telemetry support a spaceflight simulator; no separate narrative/progression evidence warrants adding Adventure.

title: Word Ladder Duel
mechanics: Word-chain puzzle: both players change exactly one letter while preserving word length and avoiding repeats. First-party options explicitly include same-device play, play against a bot, and a private room.

actions: Selected T to turn WALK into TALK and submitted the tutorial word.
gameplay.outcome: The tutorial advanced from the WALK-to-TALK instruction to 'Now it is the other player's turn. Turn TALK into TALL by replacing its last letter.' This verifies a valid one-letter word change and turn progression. The match setup also explicitly exposes Same device and Private room modes; no online room was created.
limitations: Only the tutorial step was played; no full match, bot match, or private/online room was started.

sources.detail: The live tutorial displays the WALK-to-TALK word change and advances to the other player's turn; the setup explicitly lists Same device, Play the bot, and Private room.

rationale: Puzzle is the core word-transformation mechanic. Multiplayer is supported because the first-party menu explicitly offers same-device play and the tutorial advances to another player's turn; this tag does not imply that a live online match was tested.

title: Night Cruise
mechanics: Open-ended night driving simulator: choose a map and vehicle, then drive an expressway without a race or mission. Vehicle stats and a live speedometer are provided.

actions: Selected Play, chose the default Japan/K1 Loop map, and selected the default Street Compact vehicle.
Held W for 1,000 ms in the driving scene.
gameplay.outcome: The in-game speedometer changed from 0 km/h to 22 km/h after W; the scene shows the car in the expressway/parking area. The first-party title screen explicitly says 'No race, no mission: pick a car, get on the expressway and drive.'
limitations: Only default map/vehicle and acceleration were tested; handling, collisions, online features, and any other modes were not tested.

sources.detail: Title screen states there is no race or mission and describes free expressway driving; the garage provides vehicle specifications and the live scene exposes a speedometer.

rationale: Replace Racing with Simulators: the creator explicitly describes an open drive with no race/time course, and the tested activity is accelerating a car on an expressway.
